Review date: 2026-08-07. Package version reviewed: TaxaFlag 0.1.0. Review conducted by
Claude Code, using the template in `inst/Code and Domain Review 2.Rmd` (the TaxaID-root
copy). This review combines findings and fixes in one pass (no separate response
document), matching the convention already used for `TaxaFetch`/`TaxaLikely`/`TaxaMatch`.

`devtools::check()`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes (was 1 warning -- a broken `\link{}`
target, fixed below). `devtools::test()`: 415 expectations (up from 382 before this
review, plus 5 expected warnings from tests deliberately checking warning messages), 0
failures.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Code Review

Purpose: To produce high quality code that is well written and organized according to
best coding practices.

### [x] Functionality: The code is readable, organized, and efficient.

Readable and consistently organized across all 10 files -- roxygen documentation,
internal-helper naming (`.` prefix), and `package::function()` cross-package calls follow
the same conventions throughout. `review_spatial_context.R` and `review_assignments.R`
are large (964/1281 lines) but that reflects real, non-duplicated surface area (a Shiny
gadget; a multi-context LLM prompt builder with retry logic) rather than disorganization
-- each is internally well-sectioned with clear internal helper boundaries.

One real base-R name collision found and fixed (see File-specific comments): `df` was
used as the primary parameter name in four exported functions (`flag_contaminant()`,
`flag_handler()`, `review_assignments()`, `review_spatial_context()`) and three internal
helpers, shadowing `stats::df()` (the F-distribution density function). Every other
package in this ecosystem already made this exact fix (`TaxaTools::create_taxon_names()`'s
`df` -> `input_df`; `TaxaHabitat`'s five functions' `data` -> `occurrence_data`) --
renamed here the same way, for consistency and to close the last package in the ecosystem
still carrying this pattern.

### [x] Optimizations: No areas needing optimization; one missing dependency declaration found and fixed.

No performance concerns -- nothing in this package does bulk/iterative work at a scale
where an algorithmic change would matter (`check_gbif_tile_range()`'s tile-fetch/patch-growth
cost is already analyzed and capped in its own roxygen; `review_assignments()`'s
LLM-batching/retry logic is already the expensive step, and is already designed to
minimize redundant calls).

`DESCRIPTION` had no `Depends: R (>= 4.1.0)` despite three files
(`build_review_covariates.R`, `compute_local_occurrence_distance.R`,
`review_spatial_context.R`) using the native pipe `|>` (R >= 4.1.0 syntax) -- confirmed via
`devtools::build()`, which emits an explicit `NB: this package now depends on R (>= 4.1.0)`
message for exactly this reason. `TaxaHabitat`/`TaxaLikely`/`TaxaTools` already carry this
same `Depends:` line for the identical reason; added here to match.

### [x] Coding standards: One real doc-accuracy bug found and fixed; otherwise no bad practices.

Every exported function has complete roxygen (title, `@param` for every argument,
`@return` describing actual structure, `@examples`). `add_posthoc_assessment()`'s and
several other files' roxygen carry substantial narrative about *why* a design choice was
made (real-data numbers, rejected alternatives, session history) rather than a terser
user-facing docstring alone -- verbose, but consistently applied across the whole
ecosystem and accurate in every instance checked; not treated as a defect.

**Real bug: broken `\link{}` cross-reference, present for many sessions.**
`build_review_covariates.R`'s roxygen referenced `\code{\link{model_review_classification}}`
twice (in `@description` and `@seealso`) -- no such function exists anywhere in this
package (confirmed via `grep -r` across `R/`, `man/`, `tests/`). This produced a real
`devtools::check()` WARNING (`Missing link(s) in Rd file`) that the package's own
`CLAUDE.md` session notes had referred to as "1 pre-existing unrelated warning+note in
`build_review_covariates.R`" across dozens of sessions without ever being resolved.
Fixed by rewording both references to plain prose (no dedicated
`model_review_classification()` wrapper exists in this package yet -- a user fits their
own model directly on this function's output).

### [x] Automated tests: Confirmed passing when run locally; one real coverage gap found and closed.

`devtools::test()`: 415 expectations, 0 failures (up from 382).

**Coverage gap: `build_review_covariates()` was the only exported function in the
package with zero test coverage** (confirmed: no `test-build_review_covariates.R`
existed, and no other test file called it). Added
`tests/testthat/test-build_review_covariates.R` (22 expectations) covering the field-side
aggregates, the two distinct "no data" cases (control-only detection vs. entirely absent
from `reads_df`, which the function's own docs say are deliberately NOT treated the same
way), the `contaminant_df`/`extra_covariate_cols` join paths, `sequence_col = NULL`,
inconsistent-sequence-length handling, `read_quantile` edge behavior, and all seven input-
validation errors. Every expected value in the new tests was checked against the real
function's live output before being written into an assertion, not derived by reading the
source alone.

### [x] Vulnerabilities: No exploitable vulnerabilities found.

This package's only network-facing code (`check_gbif_tile_range()`,
`compute_local_occurrence_distance()`'s pure-arithmetic path, `review_spatial_context()`'s
gadget) either takes no untrusted external input (GBIF/iNaturalist URLs are built from a
caller-supplied `taxon_key`/coordinates typed by the analyst running the script, not from
any external or multi-user input path) or uses `httr2::req_url_query()` (which
URL-encodes correctly) for the one place a free-text taxon name is sent
(`.resolve_gbif_taxon_key()`). `review_assignments()`'s LLM prompt construction has no
code-execution path back from the LLM response -- `.parse_review_response()` only ever
parses the response as JSON into a data frame of plain string fields, never `eval()`s or
sources anything from it.

One minor robustness note, not a vulnerability: `.gbif_tile_url()` (internal,
`review_spatial_context.R`) interpolates the caller-supplied `style`/`year_range`
arguments into a URL template via `sprintf()` without URL-encoding. Not exploitable (these
are R function arguments the analyst running the gadget supplies directly, not data from
any external or multi-user source), but noted in case this function is ever exposed to a
less-trusted caller in the future -- `httr2::req_url_query()` (already used elsewhere in
this same file) would be the safer construction.

Any Additional comments, list below in comment section.

None beyond the file-specific comments below.

# Domain Review

Purpose: To ensure the code produces outputs, data, interfaces, or software that is
biologically reasonable when compared to other similar information available. Review
should be conducted by someone with applicable subject-matter knowledge.

### [x] Scientific Rigor

No physical/biological constants are used in this package (it operates on already-scored
detections/read counts/timestamps, not raw measurements), so there is no "density of
granite"-class check to make. The one statistical mechanism with real domain content --
`flag_contaminant()`'s depth-weighted, Empirical-Bayes-shrunk contamination score -- is
already extensively documented and empirically validated in its own roxygen (`Session
151`/`152` real-data validation against PtConception 12S/18S datasets, including two
rejected alternative designs and why each failed); nothing found in this review contradicts
that record. `check_gbif_tile_range()`'s Web Mercator georeferencing math and GBIF tile-size
assumptions (512px `@1x.png`, not the 256px slippy-map convention) are documented as
empirically verified against live tiles, not assumed -- re-derived independently during
this review and confirmed consistent with the standard Web Mercator ground-resolution
formula.

### [x] Outputs

Outputs are internally consistent with the rest of the TaxaID ecosystem's documented
conventions (the `observation_validity`/`validity_flag`/`validity_reason` schema shared
between `flag_contaminant()` and `flag_handler()`; the Axis 1/Axis 2 columns
`add_posthoc_assessment()` appends match `TaxaAssign::posterior_consensus()`'s real output
column names). No equation-transcription errors found.

### [x] Algorithms

Found and fixed one real correctness bug (below): `flag_handler()`'s use of base R
`merge()` did not preserve input row order, silently misaligning the appended
`observation_validity`/`validity_flag`/`validity_reason`/`edge_anchor_source` columns
against the original data whenever `group_col` groups appeared in the input in a
non-alphabetical order. This is exactly the class of bug this ecosystem's own `merge()`
usage elsewhere (e.g. `review_assignments.R`'s own `.join_key` merge, which already tracks
a row index and re-sorts afterward) was written specifically to avoid -- `flag_handler()`
was the one place in the package that hadn't adopted that pattern.

Every other filtering/aggregation step reviewed (the depth-weighted rate computation in
`.compute_contaminant_scores()`, the tile-mosaic stitching/8-connected patch growth in
`check_gbif_tile_range()`, the haversine distance in `compute_local_occurrence_distance()`)
uses standard, appropriately-applied techniques for its stated purpose, with edge cases
(zero-read rows, `NA` coordinates, HTTP 204 empty tiles) handled explicitly rather than
silently mishandled.

Any Additional comments, list below in comment section.

None.

# File specific comments

**flag_handler.R**

* [x] reviewed

- **Real bug, fixed**: `merge(df, group_edges, by = ".tmp_group", all.x = TRUE)` used
  base R's default `sort = TRUE`, which re-sorts the output by the join key
  (`.tmp_group`) -- for any input with more than one `group_col` value in
  non-alphabetical row order, this silently reorders the returned data frame relative to
  the input, even though this function's own documented contract is "the input data frame
  with four columns appended." Fixed by adding an explicit `.row_id`, calling `merge(...,
  sort = FALSE)`, and re-sorting by `.row_id` afterward -- the exact pattern
  `review_assignments()`'s own `.join_key` merge already uses for the identical reason.
  New regression test (`"row order is preserved when group order is not alphabetical"`)
  added -- the pre-existing "min/max computed per group" test could never have caught this,
  since its two-group fixture happened to already be in alphabetical order (`StationA`
  before `StationB`).
- `df` renamed to `input_df` (shadows `stats::df()`) -- see Code Review's Functionality
  section.

**flag_contaminant.R**

* [x] reviewed

- `df` renamed to `input_df` throughout (public function + internal
  `.compute_contaminant_scores()`).
- No other issues found. `.compute_contaminant_scores()`'s roxygen is unusually long for
  an internal (`@noRd`) helper, but it is the load-bearing record of *why* the
  depth-weighting/shrinkage design looks the way it does (including two rejected
  alternatives found to fail on real data) -- kept as-is.

**review_assignments.R**

* [x] reviewed

- `df` renamed to `input_df` throughout (public function; internal helpers already used
  `df` only as a generic second parameter, also renamed for consistency).
- `.build_candidate_label()`'s roxygen already documents that it deliberately duplicates
  `TaxaAssign::.make_slash_name()`'s logic rather than depending on `TaxaAssign` -- a
  documented, deliberate DRY trade-off (avoiding a hard package dependency for one small
  helper), not an oversight; left as-is.
- No functional issues found. The truncated-JSON recovery path
  (`.recover_truncated_json()`) and the halve-and-retry batching logic
  (`.review_batch_with_retry()`) are both exercised by dedicated tests, including the real
  failure mode that motivated the parenthetical-rank-annotation stripping in
  `.parse_review_response()` (documented inline as a real 2026-07-14 production bug, not
  hypothetical).

- This is a live, actively-iterated Shiny/leaflet gadget (nine real click-through rounds

**add_posthoc_assessment.R**

* [x] reviewed

**TaxaFlag-package.R**

# Not fixed (out of scope for this pass)

- `TaxaWizard/inst/metadata/TaxaFlag.json`'s `add_posthoc_assessment` entry still
  describes the pre-2026-07-30 design (a single `posthoc_assessment` column driven by
  `tiers`/`finest_rank`), superseded by the current Axis 1/Axis 2 (`primary_plausibility`/
  `primary_discrimination`/etc.) redesign. This is pre-existing drift unrelated to
  anything touched in this review (confirmed via `git log` -- last touched Session 104,
  2026-06-08, well before the 2026-07-30 redesign) and TaxaWizard's own `CLAUDE.md`
  documents this class of metadata drift as a known, separately-tracked issue
  (`[[project_taxawizard_metadata_drift]]`). The three `"name": "df"` entries this review
  *did* touch (`flag_contaminant`/`flag_handler`/`review_assignments`) were fixed since
  they were a direct, mechanical consequence of the rename made here.
